([[North Vancouver (district municipality)|North Vancouver]], [[British Columbia]]) | college = [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2007–2012) | draft_year = 2012 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 60 | draft_team = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | career_start = 2012 | career_end = 2019 | career_position = [[Center (basketball)|Center]] | career_number = 50, 6 | years1 = {{nbay|2012|start}}–{{nbay|2015|end}} | team1 = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | years2 = 2012–2013 | team2 = →[[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] | years3 = 2017–2019 | team3 = [[Hitachi SunRockers Tokyo-Shibuya]] | highlights = *2× First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2011, 2012) *WCC Defensive Player of the Year (2012) | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|CAN}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA AmeriCup]]}} {{MedalBronze| [[2015 FIBA Americas Championship|2015 Mexico City]] | }} }} '''Robert Sacre''' (born June 6, 1989) is a Former American-Canadian professional [[basketball]] player who is the assistant general manager for the [[Vancouver Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL). A [[dual citizen]] of the United States and Canada,{{cite news|first=Bruce |last=Pascoe |url=http://www.azcentral.com/sports/ua/articles/2011/12/16/20111216arizona-wildcats-basketball-gonzaga-preview.html |title=Arizona Wildcats basketball set to face Gonzaga |newspaper=Arizona Daily Star |date=December 16, 2011 |access-date=December 16, 2011 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130117133726/http://www.azcentral.com/sports/ua/articles/2011/12/16/20111216arizona-wildcats-basketball-gonzaga-preview.html?nclick_check=1 |archive-date=January 17, 2013 |url-status=live }} he has played for the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian national basketball team]]. After playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]], he was selected by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] with the last overall pick in the second round of the [[2012 NBA draft]]. He played four seasons with the Lakers and three seasons with the [[Sun Rockers Shibuya]] in Japan. ==Early life== Sacre was born in the United States in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]] to former [[National Football League]] player [[Greg LaFleur]] and former [[LSU Lady Tigers basketball|LSU Lady Tigers]] college basketball player Leslie Sacre.{{cite news|first=Eric|last=Duhatschek|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/last-pick-looking-to-become-second-canuck-on-lakers-celebrated-roster/article4677851/|title=Last pick looking to become second Canuck on Lakers celebrated roster|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=October 26, 2012|access-date=November 1, 2012|quote=Sacre, who was born in Baton Rouge, La., comes by his athletic pedigree honestly.}} His mother, a Canadian, moved back to Canada when Sacre was seven, and raised her son as a single mother. Sacre grew up in [[North Vancouver (district municipality)|North Vancouver]], [[British Columbia]], and he was {{convert|6|ft|8|in|m}} by the eighth grade. Leslie only insisted that he learn to swim, and she did not push him to play basketball.{{cite news|first=Gare |last=Joyce |url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/2012/02/10/sportsnet_magazine_gonzaga/ |title=CanCon leading charge for Gonzaga |magazine=Sportsnet Magazine |date=February 10, 2012 |access-date=February 10, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130115133226/http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/2012/02/10/sportsnet_magazine_gonzaga/ |archive-date=January 15, 2013 |url-status=dead }} Sacre was one of the top high school players in Canada. In his junior year, he led [[Handsworth Secondary School]] to the British Columbia Provincial Championship; he was named MVP of the title game after scoring 17 points, grabbing 12 rebounds, and blocking four shots.{{cite web|url=http://www.gozags.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26400&ATCLID=205173769 |title=Robert Sacre Biography |work=GoZags.com |access-date=January 9, 2017 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150206190535/http://www.gozags.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=26400&ATCLID=205173769 |archive-date=February 6, 2015 }} In that same year he was selected to play for the Canadian Junior National team at the 2005 Global Games and the 2006 World Championship qualifiers. In his senior year he averaged 25 points, 12 rebounds, and four and a half blocks per game. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Sacre was listed as the No. 10 center and the No. 102 player in the nation in 2007.{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/43922|title=Robert Sacre Recruiting Profile|work=Rivals.com|access-date=January 9, 2017}} ==College career== [[File:Robert Sacre Gonzaga.jpg|thumb|right|Sacre takes a hook shot while playing for [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]]]] Sacre committed to [[NCAA]] Division I squad [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga University]] prior to the 2007–08 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/6620/robert-sacre|title=Robert Sacre Stats, Bio|work=ESPN.com|access-date=January 9, 2017}} He came off the bench in his freshman season, averaging nine minutes of action per game in 2007–08. In 2008–09, he broke his foot three games into the season and was later granted a medical redshirt. Sacre came back strong in the 2009–10 season, averaging 10.3 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game as the Bulldogs' starting centre. In 2012, Sacre finished his career with 1,270 points. He also grabbed 679 career rebounds and had 186 career blocks. ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Lakers (2012–2016)=== [[File:Robert Sacre Lakers 2013.jpg|thumb|upright|Sacre during the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]]] On June 28, 2012, the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] selected Sacre with the last pick (60th) in the [[2012 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Rosales|url=http://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2012/6/29/3125267/draft-night-2012-lakers-select-darius-johnson-odom-robert-sacre|title=Draft Night 2012: Lakers Select Darius Johnson-Odom, Robert Sacre|work=SilverScreenAndRoll.com|publisher=SB-Nation|date=June 29, 2012|access-date=January 9, 2017}} After joining the Lakers for the [[2012 NBA Summer League]],{{cite web|first=Peter|last=Emerick|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1253621-la-lakers-summer-league-roster-key-storylines|title=Los Angeles Lakers: Summer League Roster, Key Storylines|work=BleacherReport.com|date=July 10, 2012|access-date=January 9, 2017}} he signed with the Lakers on September 7.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/120907lakers-sign-robert-sacre|title=Lakers Sign Robert Sacre|work=NBA.com|date=September 7, 2012|access-date=September 7, 2012}} On October 31, he made his NBA debut against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], playing 49 seconds in a 116–106 loss. He scored his first points on November 4, 2012, in a victory against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. On January 8, 2013, Sacre made his first career start, finishing with 10 points, four blocked shots and three rebounds in a 125–112 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400278234|title=James Harden scores 31 as surging Rockets pick up 5th straight win|work=ESPN.com|date=January 8, 2013|access-date=January 9, 2013}} During his rookie season, he had multiple assignments with the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 9, 2013|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|url-status=dead}} On July 10, 2013, Sacre re-signed with the Lakers to a three-year deal{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/130710sacre_re_sign|title=Lakers Re-Sign Robert Sacre|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=July 12, 2013}}{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Pincus|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-xpm-2013-jul-12-la-sp-ln-lakers-robert-sacre-20130712-story.html|title=Robert Sacre under contract for three more seasons with Lakers|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=July 12, 2013}} and joined them for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/2013_summer|title=Lakers 2013 Summer League Roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2013|access-date=January 9, 2017}} On February 5, 2014, Sacre was involved in a bizarre game after receiving his sixth foul during a game against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. The Lakers had dressed eight players, losing guards [[Jordan Farmar]] and [[Nick Young (basketball)|Nick Young]] to injury during the course of the game. With [[Chris Kaman]] having already fouled out and coach [[Mike D'Antoni]] electing not to play [[Steve Nash]], the Lakers roster had been trimmed down to four eligible players after Sacre committed his sixth foul. In accordance to league rules, Sacre was allowed to stay in the game after being assessed a technical foul on top of the sixth personal foul he committed.{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Harper|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/with-zero-bench-left-the-lakers-still-close-out-the-cavaliers/|title=With zero bench left, the Lakers still close out the Cavaliers|work=CBSSports.com|date=February 5, 2014|access-date=February 5, 2014}} On September 22, 2016, Sacre signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/pelicans-sign-chris-copeland-and-robert-sacre|title=Pelicans Sign Chris Copeland and Robert Sacre|work=NBA.com|date=September 22, 2016|access-date=September 22, 2016}} However, he was later waived by the Pelicans on October 21 after appearing in one preseason game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-dawson-sacre|title=Pelicans Waive Dawson, Sacre|work=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2016|access-date=October 21, 2016}} === Sun Rockers Shibuya (2017–2019) === On January 7, 2017, Sacre signed with [[Hitachi SunRockers Tokyo-Shibuya]] of the assistant general manager for the [[Fraser Valley Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL).{{Cite web|title=Former NBAer Robert Sacre takes on new challenge with Fraser Valley Bandits|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/former-nbaer-robert-sacre-takes-new-challenge-fraser-valley-bandits/|access-date=February 16, 2022|website=SportsNet}} ==National team career== Sacre played several tournaments for the Canadian junior team. He averaged 9 points, 8.2 rebounds, and 3 blocks per game at the 2006 [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]], helping the Canadians to a fourth-place finish in the tournament.{{cite web|url=http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/56482/pid2//sid/3931/tid/257/tid2//_/2006_FIBA_Americas_U18_Championship_for_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20120802123909/http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/56482/pid2//sid/3931/tid/257/tid2//_/2006_FIBA_Americas_U18_Championship_for_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 2, 2012|title=Robert Sacre's profile – 2006 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|work=FIBA.com|access-date=January 9, 2017}} Sacre was called to the senior national team for the first time to participate at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] in Turkey.{{cite web|url=http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/10/fwcm/player/p/eid/4728/pid/56482/rid//sid/4728/tid/257/profile.html|archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20120802033820/http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/10/fwcm/player/p/eid/4728/pid/56482/rid//sid/4728/tid/257/profile.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=August
